macro_blurb: Geopolitics dominates the tape: reporting indicates Trump is "not rushing" an Iran deal while dismissing critics, leaving negotiations open-ended, and a US medical supply CEO flagged the oil-price shock tied to Strait of Hormuz risk — a direct channel into energy-sensitive European and US sectors. The Ukraine front escalated as Moscow struck Ukraine with the Oreshnik missile, adding a fresh layer to defense and energy risk premia in EU markets. In the EU, Cyprus's parliamentary shift to the right delivered a setback to the president, a reminder of fragmenting coalitions on the bloc's periphery. Sector-specific flow: Uber is reportedly weighing a higher bid for Delivery Hero, and the ECB has summoned banks to address weaknesses exposed by the latest AI models.
synthesis:
Today's screen is unmistakably an EU yield-and-value print: 8 of 10 picks are European, the average Yield percentile sits at 91, Value at 84, and Momentum at 85, while Quality lags at 72. Six names carry dividend yields above 5.7%, four above 6.2%. No single sector dominates — Utilities and Industrials tie at two apiece — but the factor signature is uniform: cheap multiples, fat payouts, three-month moves well ahead of sector medians. The composite range (75.9 to 100) is tight, meaning conviction is broad rather than concentrated in a single name.

Three picks tell the same story: Teleperformance (TEP.PA), Signify (LIGHT.AS) and Enagás (ENG.MC) all combine top-decile Yield with sub-14x P/Es and FCF yields between 0.1% and 25% — the European "high-payout, suspect-quality" trade, where the market is paying you to hold structural question marks. Edenred (EDEN.PA) and Vallourec (VK.PA) extend it with 22% and 24% three-month moves. The Oreshnik strike and Hormuz-linked oil shock reinforce the energy-and-defense risk premium that's been lifting Enagás and Vallourec specifically.

The outlier is Covestro (1COV.DE) at composite 100 — negative ROE, negative FCF yield, trading on ADNOC deal mechanics, not fundamentals. Conspicuously absent: Energy (despite the Hormuz tape), Healthcare, Real Estate and Consumer Cyclical — zero picks across four sectors from 826 scored names. Watch the EU ruling on the ADNOC/Covestro bid and any concrete Iran-deal movement; either flips the energy premium underwriting half this list.
